title: Associate General Counsel
description:
About EnergyHub

EnergyHub empowers utilities and their customers to create a clean, distributed energy future. We help consumers turn their smart thermostats, EVs, batteries, and other products into virtual power plants that keep the grid stable and enable higher penetration of solar and wind power.

About the Opportunity

EnergyHub seeks an Associate General Counsel to join its expanding legal team. EnergyHub empowers utilities and their customers to create a clean, distributed energy future by helping consumers turn their smart thermostats, EVs, batteries, and other products into virtual power plants that keep the grid stable and enable higher penetration of solar and wind power. The Associate General Counsel will work hand-in-hand with EnergyHub’s business leaders and technical teams to help the company continue its high growth rate and achieve its goal of a carbon-free, distributed energy future.

The Associate General Counsel will work with teams across EnergyHub to provide advice on a wide range of legal matters, including commercial contracts and transactions, privacy, IP, compliance, M&A, and regulatory issues as well as general corporate matters. The legal team supports all aspects of EnergyHub’s business operations, including commercial relationships, intellectual property, and strategic activities. If you’re excited about interacting with all aspects of a high-growth software business and being on the cutting edge of climate tech, this might be the job for you.

Main Responsibilities: What you'll do

  • Draft, review, and negotiate a wide range of agreements for EnergyHub, including software, technology, services, vendor, reseller, manufacturer, licensing, marketing and other commercial contracts. A significant portion of time in this position will be spent working with leading companies in the demand response, climate tech, Internet of Things, renewable energy, and utility sectors, and partnering with EnergyHub’s internal teams to define a broad legal and risk management strategy and develop creative solutions to legal issues involved with deploying its industry-leading software platform.
  • Advise and provide guidance on a broad scope of legal issues relating to commercial terms, compliance, privacy, security, and regulatory matters
  • Work closely with executive, sales, IT, product, and other business teams to provide general legal advice and support and assist in scaling legal and business processes
  • Work collaboratively with the EnergyHub/Alarm.com legal team and manage legal staff
  • Develop and drive compliance policies and procedures designed to enhance regulatory and business standards compliance and support the company’s business and strategic objectives
  • Supervise and coordinate with outside counsel as necessary
  • Manage internal paralegal resources as necessary
  • Other duties as assigned

Required Skills and Experience: What you need

  • 5+ years relevant experience in an in-house or large law firm environment, with software, technology industry experience. Familiarity with one or more of the following areas a plus: commercial contracts, public utilities, IP, data and privacy or other regulatory frameworks
  • Significant experience negotiating, drafting and reviewing broad range of commercial contracts and familiarity with a wide range of legal matters including corporate, commercial, privacy, IP, regulatory, and compliance issues; demonstrated ability/interest in becoming a corporate generalist
  • Team player with a high level of professionalism and commitment to developing strong relationships with colleagues, internal clients, and business teams across the enterprise.
  • Ability to work under pressure, juggle multiple projects with competing priorities, meet deadlines, and adapt to change within a growing company
  • Experience with, and enthusiasm for, process improvement, and problem solving
  • Superior interpersonal and written and oral communication skills
  • Proven organizational, analytical, and negotiation skills with exceptional attention to detail
  • Highly skilled in standard office software and ability to adapt quickly to new technologies
  • J.D. from a leading law school
  • Membership in or eligibility for admission to the New York Bar
  • Willingness to travel to Alarm.com’s HQ in the Washington, DC area on an occasional basis

title: Energy Data Scientist
description:
EnergyHub is working to enable a carbon-free, distributed energy future by seamlessly integrating enormous numbers of energy devices with the electric power grid. Our platform coordinates and collects terabytes of data from what will soon be more than 1,000,000 distributed energy devices, such as thermostats, electric vehicles and home batteries.

Coordinating and evaluating the performance of all of these devices to forecast and estimate the delivered grid value requires state-of-the-art data science, control systems and machine learning. As such, EnergyHub seeks to hire an Energy Data Scientist to join EnergyHub’s Analytics Engineering team. As an Energy Data Scientist you will work closely with other data scientists and analytics engineers to improve the models used for evaluation of our control algorithms. You will collaborate with the Data Science and Power Systems Intelligence team to understand the algorithms and optimizations used in order to improve our performance evaluation and forecasting abilities. You will also contribute to our data management software systems and will become core to the foundation of a future with carbon-free and distributed energy.

What you will do:

  • You will drive the development of M&V methodologies and data science models for more accurate and transparent evaluation of our advanced grid services from fleets of distributed energy resources.
  • You will write production-level code, prototype new data products, and apply machine learning algorithms to energy IoT data
  • You will work to translate data from one of the largest distributed energy datasets in the electricity industry into actionable insights for electric utilities and other energy industry stakeholders
  • You will collaborate closely with stakeholders inside and outside of EnergyHub including Data Engineering, Client Success, Marketing, Sales, Product, and Market Development teams.
  • Other duties as assigned

Who you are:

  • You are passionate about enabling a carbon-free, distributed energy future
  • You thoroughly enjoy finding valuable insights in large, complex datasets
  • You have experience with Python and the scientific stack (pandas, numpy, scipy)
  • You have proficiency in SQL and understand good data modeling practices (basic ETL/ELT)
  • You have a practical comprehension of basic machine learning algorithms and are familiar with popular software packages such as Sklearn and Tensorflow.
  • You can explain results from large-scale data analyses to diverse audiences in a way that is clear, interesting and actionable
  • You can have fun while working on really hard problems with really smart people

Bonus points if:

  • You have experience in the measurement and verification (M&V) of control and optimization of distributed energy resources
  • You have experience in using Snowflake, dbt and understanding analytics engineering development practices
  • You have experience with at least one BI tool such as Sigma, Tableau, Looker, etc)
  • You have experience with scaling data science products in the cloud (e.g., Databricks, AWS, GCP, Azure)
  • You have a strong background in mathematics and statistics
  • You have power systems expertise, including three-phase distribution network modeling

title: Lead Product Manager
description:
The Problem to solve

Utility systems weren't built to connect seamlessly with a DER platform. CIS holds the customer record, while ADMS and Grid DERMS drive real-time grid decisions. Each system operates with its own data model, security posture, and review process. You will be the key leader who transforms that fragmentation into a coherent, streamlined integration strategy.

The Role

As the Lead Product Manager, you will own how EnergyHub connects and integrates with utility operational systems, ensuring we understand our mutual end-customers (CIS), manage distribution grid conditions (OT systems), and unlock automation opportunities that drive value. This is a focused mandate where you will own the utility-facing integration surface end to end. Over time, your team will leverage internal APIs built by core platform teams to solve the "last-mile" challenge, building a robust set of outward connectors and an ecosystem of software vendors and system integration partners.

This role reports to a Director of Product and will collaborate with stakeholders across the company, including other product managers, engineers, data scientists, sales, solutions engineering, and client success.

Why this role matters

  • You are the technical face of EnergyHub inside utility control rooms and IT departments. Strong utility relationships depend on whether client technical teams trust and derive long-term value from our integrations.
  • Sticky integrations drive both revenue growth and client retention. Your products will save time for customers, unlock new VPP use cases on the grid, improve renewal rates, and boost post-integration NPS scores.

What you’ll do

  • Own the product roadmap for utility system integrations across CIS, ADMS, and Grid DERMS, balancing multiple integration channels to optimize investment across each.
  • Extend internal APIs outward into a polished, cohesive, and highly performant public API surface.
  • Drive enrollment automation logic to seamlessly onboard customers and their DER assets into program eligibility and lifecycle systems.
  • Accelerate customer onboarding and time-to-value through developer-friendly API usability tools, including SDKs, quick-start guides, test datasets, and clear documentation.
  • Partner with core platform teams to shape data model extensions across key domains required for platform-wide automation and analysis.
  • Translate complex utility technical constraints into clear product requirements that balance long-term platform stability with rapid deal execution.
  • Other duties as assigned.

What you bring

  • 8+ years of software product management experience, with meaningful ownership of APIs, platform products, or third-party integrations.
  • Deep utility operations knowledge, including familiarity with systems like CIS and ADMS.
  • Comfort navigating security, compliance, and IT governance reviews alongside client technical teams.
  • A track record of taking messy, non-standard requirements from multiple stakeholders and turning them into a coherent product plan.

Strong plus

  • Direct exposure to utility control room operations, NERC CIP requirements and/or Customer Information Systems.
  • Prior experience with API products, in-house utility environments, enterprise integrations, or solutions engineering.

title: Manager, Accounting
description:
Accounting Manager

Remote – United States | Brooklyn, NY or Burlington, VT

About the Role

EnergyHub empowers utilities and their customers to build a cleaner, more distributed energy future — helping consumers turn smart thermostats, EVs, and batteries into virtual power plants that keep the grid stable and expand renewable capacity.

We're looking for an Accounting Manager to join a growing Finance team at a pivotal moment in EnergyHub's evolution. This is a role for a technically rigorous accountant who brings precision and depth to everything they touch — someone who is energized by complexity and holds the work to an uncompromising standard. You'll own the month-end close end-to-end, serve as the technical anchor of the accounting function, and have genuine influence over how our processes and reporting evolve. You'll work within a structure set by our parent company, Alarm.com (Nasdaq: ALRM), while building something that truly serves EnergyHub.

If you're passionate about technical accounting, ready to take real ownership, and want your work to matter beyond the close, this role was written for you.

What You'll Do

  • Own EnergyHub's month-end and quarter-end close — journal entries, account reconciliations, and supporting schedules prepared with accuracy and on time, within the broader schedule set by Alarm.com corporate accounting
  • Evaluate and redesign the close process from the ground up, building scalable, repeatable workflows and the documentation and controls to support them
  • Serve as the escalation point for complex or judgmental accounting matters, including revenue recognition under ASC 606
  • Partner with Alarm.com corporate accounting as EnergyHub's primary close liaison — meeting their standards for accuracy, documentation, and deadlines while translating requirements back to the EnergyHub team in a way that supports rather than impedes the business
  • Partner with EnergyHub's internal teams — operations, customer success, FP&A — to provide the accounting guidance, context, and information they need to make better decisions
  • Play a key role in EnergyHub's ERP migration — a multi-year initiative that will reshape how the accounting function operates — in partnership with Finance leadership and the broader Alarm.com project team
  • Take on additional projects as business needs evolve — this team is growing and the scope of this role will grow with it

What We're Looking For

Must-Haves

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting
  • Active CPA license
  • 6+ years of progressive accounting experience, including public accounting and close experience in a public company environment
  • Deep, working knowledge of U.S. GAAP — you find the technical side of accounting genuinely interesting, not just necessary
  • Demonstrated ability to identify process gaps and build scalable solutions
  • Strong project management, organizational, and time management skills

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience redesigning and implementing a close process and/or building management reporting packages from the ground up
  • Experience in SaaS, software, energy, or tech
  • Experience with multi-entity consolidation or a subsidiary/parent company reporting structure
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Dynamics GP (Great Plains)

How You'll Work

You hold the work to an uncompromising standard and bring deep technical knowledge to every judgment call. You don't cut corners, and you don't let ambiguity become an excuse for imprecision. When something doesn't look right, you dig in. When a policy or requirement seems unclear to a colleague, you explain the why — because you know that understanding drives better outcomes than compliance alone.

You understand that accounting doesn't happen in a vacuum. You're equally comfortable navigating the precision and rigor that a corporate accounting team demands and translating complex requirements into plain language for a team of non-accountants who need context, not just answers. You see your role as building something that supports the business — not policing it.

You're energized by the challenge of walking into a complex environment and making it better. You don't need a perfect environment to do excellent work — you build the environment.

title: Manager, Policy and Regulatory Affairs
description:
We are seeking a dynamic professional well versed in the electric utility industry to join our team as Manager, Policy and Regulatory Affairs. The ideal candidate has distributed energy resources (DER) and demand-side management expertise, and experience collaborating with a broad spectrum of industry and government stakeholders. You have the ability to translate EnergyHub's product vision into a set of regulatory and policy objectives with the power to unlock new opportunities across our business units. You are both a big picture and analytical thinker who can turn complex device and DER program data into digestible comments and thought leadership for a diverse audience. You’re motivated to interface with a wide range of stakeholders in the industry and find middle ground amongst utilities, customers, and the distributed energy community. And, you never lose sight of high-priority state, federal, and agency initiatives and proceedings with the potential to impact EnergyHub’s growth.

Besides a rock-solid work ethic and a strong team-oriented personality, we’re looking for a candidate that is creative, passionate, and has a desire to break new ground in a constantly shifting landscape.

Main Responsibilities

The Manager, Policy and Regulatory Affairs, will be an integral part of the Regulatory Affairs team, with the primary responsibilities of accelerating EnergyHub’s growth through legislative, regulatory, and other policy advocacy and providing intelligence to support clients and shape EnergyHub’s long-term business strategy. They will lead EnergyHub’s engagement in public utility commission proceedings and legislative sessions to help scale existing customer programs, and advocate for reforms that ultimately unlock the full value of demand flexibility. The Manager, Policy and Regulatory Affairs will report to the Director of Regulatory Affairs and will collaborate with teams across the company to ensure that our advocacy reflects all that EnergyHub has to offer.

Specifically, you will:

  • Help develop and execute our regulatory and legislative engagement strategies for the central and eastern United States, with a particular focus on Midwest markets (e.g., Illinois, Ohio, Michigan, and neighboring states).

title: Software Engineer I
description:
About the job

We are looking for a Software Engineer to join the Kapacity.io team at EnergyHub!

Our team, made up of YC alumni (S21) and elite product and software talent, builds some of the most advanced flexibility solutions in the market.

Kapacity.io, previously backed by Y Combinator and acquired by EnergyHub in 2024, focuses on the European energy market, offering an energy management platform to energy companies, allowing them to connect residential heat pumps, EVs and batteries to a Virtual Power Plant. EnergyHub is the leading residential Virtual Power Plant provider in North America, with over 2.5 million connected residential devices.

VPPs reduce the need for peak power generation, reducing investment needs and carbon emissions of the grid. title: Staff Software Engineer, Data and Partner Platform
description:
About the Opportunity

We are looking for a full-stack Staff Software Engineer to join our Data and Partner Platform team (DAP) and help shape the future of energy technology. In this role, you will operate at the intersection of deep technical craft and broad organizational impact - driving architectural decisions, mentoring engineers, and building systems that are reliable, scalable, and grounded in the realities of the energy industry. You will be a key technical voice across engineering and a trusted partner to product, operations, and business teams alike.

The Data and Partner Platform team manages partner integrations, data translation, and our Snowflake account. We work closely with most teams across the organization and drive critical platform engineering that runs core business functionality. The team is driven, diverse, and wildly talented. We are driving foundational improvements that improve our agility and speed while maintaining legacy systems.

Main Responsibilities

Technical leadership and vision

  • Champion long-term excellence by envisioning ideal approaches to complex processes and translating the vision into well-scoped, measurable initiatives that can be prioritized alongside business goals.
  • Coordinate across engineering teams to align on technical direction, standards, and best practices.
  • Develop deep domain expertise in utility programs, demand responses, DER lifecycles, wholesale energy markets, and the regulatory realities that shape them, so every technical decision is grounded in how the energy industry actually operates.
  • Collaborate with product and engineering leadership to strike the right balance between business-driven and team-driven priorities, maximizing both velocity and reliability.
  • Build the absolutely coolest stuff of your career and give yourself something to be deeply proud of.

Systems design and data engineering

  • Architect and implement scalable systems for ingesting, processing, observing, and maintaining billions of data points, with performance, accuracy, security, and compliance considered across the full lifecycle.
  • Lead schema design and data flow architecture through a collaborative and inclusive process.
  • Design and build integrations with partner and third party APIs, including OEMs, utility, and data partners, as well as file-driven pipelines (CSV/SFTP/Airflow) that support them.
  • Build and maintain microservices and APIs that other teams confidently depend on, using contract-driven development practices.

Operational excellence and incident response

  • Drive investigations end to end, from initial alert through root cause analysis to resolution, with the composure to lead under pressure and the rigor to prevent recurrence.
  • Build operational scripts, runbooks, and detection tooling that transform one-time triage into repeatable capability for the team.
  • Pursue root causes beyond their symptoms, never accepting "it's working now” without a clear understanding of why it failed and what prevents it from happening again.
  • Monitor cloud costs across the team’s toolset to maintain efficiency and justify expenditure.

Cross functional collaboration and mentorship

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with partner teams across engineering, partner solutions, and business development, leveraging trust to solve cross-team problems no single group could address alone.
  • Mentor and develop engineers across the team and broader organization while remaining open to learning from their experiences and perspectives.
  • Manage access and roles across the stack to deliver predictable, compliant experiences that meet privacy and security requirements.
  • Contribute to product quality by building new features, improving existing ones, and retiring deprecated functionality.

Key Skills & Experience

Engineering craft

  • 7+ years of professional software engineering experience with demonstrated staff-level responsibilities or equivalent scope
  • Proven full-stack engineering background with experience scaling distributed systems and designing solidly-architected microservices
  • Strong proficiency with gRPC/protobuf, RESTful APIs, and contract driven development across multi-repository service meshes.
  • Clear understanding of the distinction between OLAP and OLTP relational databases, with hands-on experience planning and implementing high-performance data processes using both.
  • Demonstrated experience integrating complex partner and third party APIs as well as building and maintaining file-driven data pipelines.
  • Rigor in UI implementation end-to-end data privacy and security

Engineering instincts

  • Relentless drive for quality and performance, with strong testing discipline spanning unit, integration, TDD, and end to end approaches.
  • Proactive approach to observability. You ensure the right context surfaces in exceptions and logs to enable rapid and accurate troubleshooting.
  • Strong data-integrity instincts and incident-response composure, with the ability to lead high-severity, multi-system investigations from first alert to final root cause.
  • Experience in support-adjacent roles including on-call rotations, triage, or customer facing resolution that has provided you empathy for how systems fail and how users get stuck.
  • Thoughtful, judicious use of AI/LLM tooling to improve efficiency without over-reliance.

Communication and presence

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. You have a talent for producing clear, concise design documents, data model references, and runbooks that become team-standard reference material.
  • Ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy while providing technical vision and guiding the team toward scalable, well-considered solutions.
  • Collaborative, warm, and generous with colleagues, with a genuine investment in helping others succeed.

Nice to haves

  • Prior experience in the energy industry, including familiarity with utility programs, demand response, DER management, or wholesale energy markets.
  • Experience working in regulated industries with compliance and data privacy requirements.
  • Background in building internal developer tooling, platform capabilities, or shared infrastructure that improves team-wide productivity.
  • Familiarity with data quality monitoring and observability tooling.

Technologies we use

We embrace modern technology and are excited to grow our stack collaboratively. For this role, we're looking for strong familiarity with the majority of these technologies and solid expertise in several:

  • AWS, S3, SNS/SQS, RabbitMQ
  • Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran, Postgres, and MongoDB
  • gRPC/protobuf, React, TypeScript, Java, Spring Boot, Python
  • DataDog, Metaplane
  • Airflow, Docker, Robot Framework
  • Sigma
  • GitHub

Please note that sponsorship of new applicants for employment authorization, or any other immigration-related support, is not available for this position at this time.

Why work for EnergyHub?

  • Collaborate with outstanding people: Our employees work hard, do great work, and enjoy collaborating and learning from each other.
  • Make an immediate impact: New employees can expect to be given real responsibility for bringing new technologies to the marketplace. You are empowered to perform as soon as you join the team!
  • Gain well rounded experience: EnergyHub offers a diverse and dynamic environment where you will get the chance to work directly with executives and develop expertise across multiple areas of the business.
  • Work with the latest technologies: You'll gain exposure to a broad spectrum of IoT, SaaS and machine learning obstacles, including distributed fault-tolerance, device control optimization, and process modeling to support scalable interaction with disparate downstream APIs.
  • Be part of something important: Help create the future of how energy is produced and consumed. Make a positive impact on our climate.

About EnergyHub

EnergyHub empowers utilities and their customers to create a clean, distributed energy future. We help consumers turn their smart thermostats, EVs, batteries, and other products into virtual power plants that keep the grid stable and enable higher penetration of solar and wind power.

To learn more, visit energyhub.com.
